domain_label: Content Engineering — Academic-Book Decomposition (book -> units -> terms -> claims -> relations -> multi-step questions -> cards)
purpose: A method for decomposing an academic textbook into a spaced-repetition deck: exploit textbook anatomy (front/back matter, chapters, learning objectives, end-of-chapter questions, glossary, index), size units and cards to the working-memory chunk limit, extract terms -> atomic claims -> relations(edges) -> multi-step questions along the revised-Bloom ladder, compile each layer into well-formed Anki card types (basic/reversed/type-in, cloze, image occlusion, edge-card families), lint the bad-card patterns, and gate the deck against the book's own end-of-chapter questions (coverage) and a per-card source trace (honesty) -- presenting BOTH a concept-graph and a flat-unit representation of the prerequisite structure because the owner is unsure about graphs, and tagging every claim FACT / ESTIMATE / UNKNOWN because this session's sources were confirmed only via search-engine snippets (direct fetch was HTTP-403 blocked).
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the source material is a conventionally-structured academic textbook (OpenStax-style: per-section learning objectives, bold key terms, chapter review, end-of-chapter review + critical-thinking questions, back-of-book glossary and index) rather than loose notes or a trade paperback

the target study tool is Anki (or an AnkiConnect-compatible scheduler) so the card-type vocabulary is Anki's built-in note types, but the decomposition pipeline is tool-agnostic above the final compile step

the research grounding was confirmed via search-engine snippets of the official pages and verbatim mirrors, not by direct fetch (supermemo.com, docs.ankiweb.net, cmap.ihmc.us and most hosts returned HTTP 403 this session), so verbatim wording of the Twenty Rules and the current Anki note-type list are carried as UNKNOWN pending a fetch-enabled verification

the owner's learning ladder (terminology -> basics -> relate two things -> those two make something else -> two/three-step thinking) is treated as the spine and mapped onto the revised Bloom process x knowledge taxonomy as the named-theory anchor
exclusions: the spaced-repetition SCHEDULING algorithm itself (SM-2 / FSRS interval math, review-load balancing) belongs to the scheduler specialist; this KB stops at emitting well-formed, source-traced cards ready to schedule
gamification, streaks, calendar/progress UI and motivation mechanics beyond the fact that flat units double as scheduler/calendar boxes
OCR / PDF-parsing and document-ingestion engineering below the level of 'parse the TOC and chapter/section boundaries'
domain-specific answer grading and the exam-blueprint mapping of a particular certification (e.g. which INBDE competencies a card serves) beyond the generic climb to Apply/Analyze
asserting the verbatim text of any Twenty-Rules heading or the full current Anki note-type list as confirmed fact when this session only had snippet-level confirmation

competency_questions.question: Which structural features of an academic textbook are machine-exploitable for decomposition, and what does each one become downstream?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TEXTBOOK_ANATOMY names the front/body/back partition and maps TOC->unit map, per-section learning objectives->Bloom-phrased unit goals, bold terms+glossary->terminology layer, end-of-chapter questions->validation set, and heavily-indexed terms->hub-node signal, tagging the OpenStax confirmation FACT and the style-manual partition ESTIMATE

competency_questions.question: What working-memory limit sizes a study unit and a card question, and why?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHUNKING_LIMITS states Miller 1956 (~7+/-2) and Cowan 2001 (~4 in the focus of attention), defines a chunk as a meaningful unit not an item count, and derives that a card question should demand <=~4 not-yet-chunked elements and a unit should introduce a handful of new concepts, with the ladder freeing slots each rung

competency_questions.question: What is the minimum information principle, how does it relate to the Twenty Rules and to Rule 17 redundancy, and why question-format at all?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MIN_INFO_PRINCIPLE states one card = one atomic fact (Wozniak Rule 4), that complex answers must be split so the scheduler grades one trace, that Rule 17 permits the SAME fact from several angles as separate simple items (redundancy is not a contradiction), and cites the testing effect (Roediger & Karpicke 2006) for why retrieval beats restudy

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the pipeline runs BOOK->UNITS->TERMS->CLAIMS->RELATIONS->MULTI-STEP->cards->gate with unit(id,objectives,pages,order), term(id,unit,name,definition,image?), claim(id,text,terms,source,date?), edge(term_a,relation,term_b,unit), and multi-step composed from 2-3 edge chains, each stage named

competency_questions.question: When is a cloze deletion the right card form and what are its quality guardrails?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLOZE_DELETION names cloze as Wozniak Rule 5 (the fastest path from text to items), gives the Anki syntax {{c1::...}} with separate cards per cloze number and nested clozes since 2.1.56, and states the guardrails: short deleted span (minimum information), remaining sentence uniquely determines the answer (interference), meaningful surrounding context

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PREREQ_MAPPING gives Option G (concept map / Knowledge Space Theory surmise relation + fringe, deployed in ALEKS) and Option F (flat units with chapter order approximating prerequisites), and GRAPH_VS_FLAT recommends the hybrid -- flat units as the scheduling spine plus a lightweight edge table (term_a, relation, term_b, unit_id) extracted anyway -- so the choice stays reversible and full KST is deferred until adaptive selection demands it

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BAD_CARD_LINT enumerates overloaded, set, enumeration, interference-pair, ambiguous, orphan and undated-volatile patterns with the documented fix each (split; set->enumeration->cloze; overlapping cloze; contrast + context cue; tighten wording; learn context + link + example; date/source stamp), and INTERFERENCE_CONTROL states interference (Rule 11/16) is a global property checked across the whole deck and constrains auto-reversed cards

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CARD_TEMPLATES maps terms->Basic / Basic-and-reversed / type-in, claims->cloze (+image occlusion where spatial), relations->edge-card family, multi-step->case cards, flags 'Basic (optional reversed)' and 'type in the answer' as snippet-unconfirmed this session, and warns to auto-reverse only when the back uniquely identifies the front (else manufactured interference)

competency_questions.question: What gate decides the decomposition is done, and what does a failure loop back to?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COVERAGE_HONESTY_GATE requires the deck to answer the book's own end-of-chapter questions (coverage oracle) and every card to trace to a claim/edge carrying a source (honesty), and routes a coverage failure back to the claim/relation extraction stage rather than patching the card

competency_questions.question: How are multi-step questions authored so a novice can learn them, and when are the scaffolds removed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WORKED_EXAMPLE_ORDERING cites Sweller & Cooper 1985 (worked examples let novices learn the schema first -- ~half the time, ~1/5 the errors) and the expertise-reversal effect (fade worked examples as expertise grows), and RELATIONS_TO_MULTISTEP writes each item with its worked solution first then a problem-only variant to fade into

competency_questions.question: How are the terminology-layer records harvested from a chapter, and what makes a good term record?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNIT_TO_TERMS harvests bold/key terms + back-of-book glossary + index hits into one record per term (id, unit_id, name, definition, image?), treats heavily-indexed terms as hub nodes, and marks this as rung-1 (Remember x Factual) material feeding the claim and edge stages

glossary.definition: Wozniak's Rule 4: formulate each item as simply as possible so one card grades one memory trace; complex answers are split into many atomic items that are answered fast, scheduled accurately and fail independently. Rule 17 complements it -- the SAME fact from several angles as separate simple items is welcome redundancy, not a violation.

A sentence with a hidden fragment the learner supplies (Wozniak Rule 5, 'easy and effective'); in Anki, hidden text is wrapped {{c1::...}} and each cloze number generates a separate card (nested clozes supported since 2.1.56). Well-formed clozes hide a short span whose remaining context uniquely determines the answer.

Occluding part of an image and asking for the masked region -- Wozniak Rule 8 ('as good as cloze deletion'), implemented natively in Anki since version 23.10 as the Image Occlusion note type (a special case of cloze on images). Best for anatomy plates, charts, maps and labeled diagrams; whether it beats an equivalent text cloze for anatomy specifically is [UNKNOWN] (no controlled card-format A/B study located).

A triple (A, relation, B) -- the concept-map proposition of Novak & Canas 2008 -- rendered as a small card family: forward (What does A <relation>? -> B), reverse only if B uniquely identifies A (Rule 11), a relation card (How are A and B related?), and a cloze form. 'Edges' is the owner's term; the equation edges~=propositions is an [ESTIMATE] mapping, high confidence.

A meaningful unit of working memory, not a raw item count: Miller 1956 put immediate memory at ~7+/-2 chunks, Cowan 2001 put the rehearsal-controlled focus-of-attention limit at ~4. Expertise is partly the building of ever-larger chunks, so each ladder rung turns the previous rung's outputs into single chunks and frees slots for the next composition.

Anderson & Krathwohl 2001: a cognitive-process dimension (Remember -> Understand -> Apply -> Analyze -> Evaluate -> Create) crossed with a knowledge dimension (Factual -> Conceptual -> Procedural -> Metacognitive). In this factory the process dimension is the ladder (what a question demands) and the knowledge dimension is the content type (what a KB entry is); a card is typed by the pair.

Doignon & Falmagne 1985: a learner's knowledge state is the set of items mastered; a surmise (prerequisite) relation constrains which states and learning paths exist; the fringe of a state -- items exactly one step ahead -- has maximal diagnostic value and is what to teach or test next. Deployed commercially in ALEKS.

A per-section goal stated at the start of each section in an OpenStax-style textbook, usually already phrased with a Bloom verb; it doubles as a ready-made unit goal and, with the end-of-chapter questions, as a target the generated deck must be able to satisfy.

The done-check on a decomposition: the deck must be able to answer the book's own end-of-chapter questions (coverage -- if it cannot, the decomposition missed content and loops back to claim extraction) and every card must trace to a claim or edge carrying a source id, with volatile facts date-stamped (honesty -- Rules 18/19).

Presenting a composed multi-step item with its full worked solution first so a novice learns the schema (Sweller & Cooper 1985: ~half the time, ~1/5 the errors versus unguided problem solving), then fading to a problem-only variant as expertise grows -- the expertise-reversal effect, which says scaffolds that help novices can hurt experts.

nodes.definition: Establish which structural features of a conventionally-structured academic textbook are machine-exploitable and what each becomes downstream. Front matter: title/copyright/TOC/preface -- the TOC is the free unit map. Body chapter skeleton (OpenStax-style makes it explicit [FACT - confirmed via OpenStax A&P front-matter snippets]): chapter intro/opening case; per-section learning objectives ('objectives stated at the beginning of each section'); sections with bold key terms, diagrams, tables; boxed clinical/example features; chapter review/summary; end-of-chapter review + critical-thinking questions, often case-based. Back matter: back-of-book glossary, appendices, references, index. Extraction leverage [ESTIMATE - synthesis, HIGH]: learning objectives ~= ready-made Bloom-phrased unit goals; bold terms + glossary ~= the terminology layer for free; end-of-chapter questions ~= a validation set (if the deck cannot answer the book's own questions, decomposition missed content); the index ~= a concept-frequency signal so heavily-indexed terms are hub nodes. The front/back-matter partition itself is standard publishing convention [ESTIMATE - not fetched from a style manual this session].

included: the front/body/back partition and the chapter skeleton
the mapping of each feature to a downstream artifact (TOC->units, objectives->goals, terms/glossary->terminology, EOC questions->validation set, index->hub signal)
the FACT/ESTIMATE tags on the OpenStax confirmation vs the style-manual partition
excluded: the actual TOC parse and unit boundaries (BOOK_TO_UNITS)

nodes.definition: Fix the working-memory limit that sizes both a study unit and a card question. Miller 1956 ('The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two') put immediate memory at ~7+/-2 chunks [FACT - snippet]; Cowan 2001 ('The magical number 4 in short-term memory'), controlling for rehearsal, put the real focus-of-attention limit at ~4 chunks [FACT - snippet]. A chunk is a meaningful unit, not an item count -- a chess master sees familiar configurations, not 32 pieces; expertise is partly the development of increasingly complex chunks. Consequences for decomposition [ESTIMATE - direct application, HIGH]: a card's question should demand <=~4 not-yet-chunked elements at once; a study unit should introduce a handful of new concepts, not dozens; the ladder works because each rung turns the last rung's items into chunks, freeing working-memory slots for the next composition. The same mechanism drives cognitive load theory and the worked-example need.

included: Miller ~7+/-2 and Cowan ~4 as the limits
chunk = meaningful unit not item count
the <=~4-element card and handful-of-concepts unit consequences and the slot-freeing ladder mechanism
excluded: the Bloom rung content of the ladder (BLOOM_LADDER)
the worked-example ordering that follows from load theory (WORKED_EXAMPLE_ORDERING)

pros.claim: A named chunk budget turns 'keep it small' into a testable size rule for units and card questions
pros.example: rejecting a card question that requires holding six unfamiliar terms at once because it exceeds the ~4-chunk focus limit

cons.claim: The limit is in chunks not items, so counting raw items misjudges load for an expert who has already chunked the material
cons.example: flagging a card as overloaded on item count when the learner has already chunked five of its elements into one

failure_modes: counting raw items instead of not-yet-chunked elements
packing a unit with dozens of new concepts against the chunk budget
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites Miller ~7+/-2 and Cowan ~4, defines a chunk as a meaningful unit, and derives the <=~4-element card and handful-of-concepts unit rules with the slot-freeing ladder mechanism
revisit_triggers: a card or unit repeatedly lapses suggesting the size budget is wrong for this material
a newer working-memory-capacity result revises the ~4 figure
the learner's expertise shifts what counts as one chunk

base.update_signal: a chronic lapse pattern or a revised capacity estimate changes the size budget

nodes.definition: Map the owner's learning ladder onto the revised Bloom taxonomy so each rung has a named theory anchor and a card form. Anderson & Krathwohl 2001 (revision of Bloom 1956) gives a cognitive-process dimension -- Remember -> Understand -> Apply -> Analyze -> Evaluate -> Create -- crossed with a knowledge dimension -- Factual -> Conceptual -> Procedural -> Metacognitive [FACT - snippets]. The mapping [ESTIMATE - design mapping, HIGH; each anchor FACT]: rung1 terminology = Remember x Factual (term cards); rung2 basics = Remember/Understand x Factual (minimum-information single facts, cloze/occlusion); rung3 relate two things = Understand x Conceptual (concept-map propositions -- the 'edges'); rung4 those two make something else = Apply x Procedural/Conceptual (worked examples -- study the composed procedure before solving); rung5 two/three-step thinking = Analyze (->Evaluate) x Conceptual (multi-step case/vignette items). The order is load-correct because each rung's outputs become single chunks at the next, keeping every question within the ~4-chunk budget; a rung-5 question asked without rung-1 vocabulary is unanswerable because every term costs a slot. Exam-style case items live mostly at Apply/Analyze, so the deck must climb there, not stop at Remember.

included: the process x knowledge dimensions of revised Bloom
the rung-by-rung mapping of the owner's ladder to (process, knowledge) pairs and card forms
the load-correctness argument and the climb-past-Remember imperative

pros.claim: Typing every card by a (process, knowledge) pair makes the deck's cognitive level explicit and forces it to climb to Apply/Analyze
pros.example: labeling an edge card (Understand, Conceptual) and a vignette (Analyze, Conceptual) so a Remember-only deck is visibly incomplete

cons.claim: The owner-ladder-to-Bloom mapping is a design mapping, so a rung can be mislabeled and mis-sequence the cards
cons.example: tagging a genuinely two-step inference as Understand and scheduling it before its prerequisite edges

failure_modes: stopping the deck at Remember/Understand and never reaching Apply/Analyze
asking a rung-5 question of a learner who lacks the rung-1 vocabulary
acceptance_tests: the analysis states both Bloom dimensions, maps each owner-ladder rung to a (process, knowledge) pair and card form, and gives the load-correctness and climb-past-Remember arguments citing Anderson & Krathwohl 2001
revisit_triggers: the exam blueprint or objective set shifts the required cognitive level
a rung is found mislabeled after cards mis-sequence
a fetch-enabled run verifies the Krathwohl 2002 level definitions

base.update_signal: an objective/exam-level shift or a mislabeled rung changes the ladder mapping

nodes.definition: Adopt Wozniak's Twenty Rules of Formulating Knowledge (SuperMemo, 1999) as the card-formulation ruleset, ordered by importance -- earlier rules are most often violated or bring most benefit [FACT - snippet of the official article]. The load-bearing rules for this factory: (1-3) do not learn what you do not understand, learn before you memorize, build upon the basics; (4) minimum information principle; (5) cloze deletion is easy and effective; (6) use imagery; (8) graphic deletion is as good as cloze; (9-10) avoid sets and enumerations (convert to enumerations then clozes); (11) combat interference; (12) optimize wording; (13) refer to other memories; (14) personalize / provide examples; (16) context cues simplify wording; (17) redundancy does not contradict minimum information; (18-19) provide sources and date-stamp volatile facts; (20) prioritize. The first ~16 rules concern making memories simple, 17-20 are meta-management [FACT - snippet]. Honesty carry: the VERBATIM heading/gloss wording of all twenty rules is [UNKNOWN] this session -- the official pages were HTTP-403 blocked and the set was reconstructed from search snippets of the article and verbatim mirrors, so exact wording must not be quoted as confirmed until a fetch-enabled run verifies it (canonical: supermemo.com/en/blog/twenty-rules-of-formulating-knowledge).

which rules drive minimum information, cloze, occlusion, sets/enumerations, interference, sourcing and dating
the UNKNOWN verbatim-wording blocker and the 403-snippet provenance

pros.example: justifying a split, a context prefix and a date stamp on one card by Rules 4, 16 and 19

nodes.definition: Operationalize the minimum information principle -- Wozniak Rule 4 -- as the atomicity discipline the whole pipeline inherits. One card = one atomic fact/relation; complex answers are split into many simple items because the scheduler grades ONE memory trace, not a bundle: simple items are answered fast, scheduled accurately and fail independently [FACT on the principle per Rule 4 snippet; the scheduling rationale is a direct consequence, ESTIMATE-HIGH]. The violation symptom is a chronically half-known card whose grade is meaningless; the fix is to split. This does NOT contradict Rule 17 -- the SAME fact from several angles as SEPARATE simple items is welcome redundancy, and reasoning/derivation steps may themselves be memorized [FACT - snippet]. Why question-format at all: the testing effect -- retrieval practice beats restudying for delayed retention (Roediger & Karpicke 2006, Test-Enhanced Learning, Psychological Science) [FACT - snippets]. Applied at the DATA level (atomic claims) so cards inherit atomicity for free rather than being split after the fact.

included: one-card-one-trace atomicity and the split fix
the Rule 17 redundancy reconciliation and derivation-step memorization
the testing-effect rationale and the apply-at-data-level discipline
excluded: the cloze mechanics that realize atomic facts (CLOZE_DELETION)

pros.claim: Enforcing atomicity at the claim level means cards are born minimum-information instead of being split after they lapse
pros.example: extracting 'the maxillary first molar has 3 roots' as one claim rather than a paragraph that later grades as one half-known bundle

cons.claim: Over-atomizing can strip the context that makes a fact meaningful, colliding with the need for a coherent structure
cons.example: shattering a mechanism into disconnected single facts so the learner never sees the relation that binds them

failure_modes: shipping an overloaded card that grades many traces as one
over-atomizing into context-free fragments that violate Rules 1-3
acceptance_tests: the analysis states one-card-one-trace with the split fix, reconciles it with Rule 17 redundancy, and cites the testing effect, prescribing atomicity at the claim/data level

base.update_signal: a half-known-card pattern or an over-atomization complaint changes the atomicity rule

nodes.definition: Treat interference as a global property of the whole deck, not a per-card defect. Wozniak Rule 11 (combat interference): similar items confuse each other and even the simplest items can be completely intractable if they are similar to other items [FACT - snippet]; Rule 16 (context cues simplify wording): a category prefix ('chem:', 'bio:') replaces long qualifying phrases and fights interference [FACT - snippet confirms concept; title wording ESTIMATE-HIGH]. The fixes: reword to maximize contrast between the confusable pair, add a discriminating context cue, sometimes add an explicit A-vs-B comparison card, and occasionally delete one item [FACT for the diagnosis; comparison-card fix ESTIMATE, medium-HIGH]. This constrains auto-reversed and edge cards: a reversed card whose 'question' is a generic definition shared by several terms manufactures interference, so only auto-reverse when the back uniquely identifies the front. Because interference is a relation BETWEEN items, the check must run across the whole deck at compile time, not on a card in isolation.

included: interference as a between-items whole-deck property (Rules 11/16)
the contrast / context-cue / comparison-card / delete fixes
the constraint on auto-reversed and edge cards and the compile-time global check

pros.claim: Checking interference across the whole deck catches confusable pairs a per-card review structurally cannot see
pros.example: flagging two drugs whose reversed cards share a near-identical definition prompt before both become intractable

cons.claim: A whole-deck interference check is a global computation that grows with deck size and can over-flag legitimately similar items
cons.example: warning on two genuinely distinct terms that merely share a word, adding noise to the lint

failure_modes: auto-reversing a card whose back is a generic shared definition
reviewing interference per-card and missing the cross-item confusion
acceptance_tests: the analysis frames interference as a between-items whole-deck property citing Rules 11/16, lists the contrast/context-cue/comparison/delete fixes, and constrains auto-reverse to backs that uniquely identify the front with a compile-time global check
revisit_triggers: a confusable pair keeps swapping answers in review
the deck grows enough that the global check needs re-running
a context-cue scheme is added or changed

base.update_signal: a recurring answer-swap or a deck-growth threshold triggers a re-run of the interference check

nodes.definition: Decide, per piece of knowledge, whether it is carried better by an image/occlusion/flowchart or by text/cloze. Evidence: the picture-superiority effect -- pictures are remembered better than words (Paivio: roughly twice as many images as words recalled after brief viewing) [FACT - snippets]; Mayer's multimedia principle -- people learn better from words + pictures than words alone, because separate visual and verbal channels share the working-memory load [FACT - snippets]. Mechanism note: recent work (Higdon et al. 2025, QJEP) argues distinctiveness, not dual coding, explains the effect -- the EFFECT is robust, the MECHANISM is debated [FACT - snippet]. Practical rule [ESTIMATE - synthesis, medium-HIGH]: use an image/occlusion card when the knowledge IS spatial or structural (anatomy, apparatus, chart positions); a flowchart occlusion when it is a decision path or sequence (clinical algorithms); text/cloze when it is verbal-symbolic (definitions, numbers, names). Caveat -- Mayer's coherence principle: decorative images add extraneous load, not memory, so an image must carry the knowledge, not merely illustrate it [FACT that the coherence principle exists - snippet].

included: the picture-superiority and multimedia evidence with the debated-mechanism honesty note
the spatial->image / sequence->flowchart / verbal->text decision rule
the coherence-principle caveat against decorative images
excluded: the cloze mechanics for the text branch (CLOZE_DELETION)

pros.claim: A medium-decision rule routes spatial knowledge to images and verbal knowledge to text instead of defaulting everything to prose
pros.example: routing a root-canal anatomy plate to image occlusion and a drug-class definition to a text cloze

cons.claim: The picture-superiority evidence is generic recall, not a card-format A/B, so the image-beats-cloze call is a reasoned default not a measured one
cons.example: assuming an occlusion card beats an equivalent text cloze for a specific anatomy fact without a controlled comparison

failure_modes: adding decorative images that raise load without carrying knowledge (coherence violation)
forcing spatial knowledge into text or verbal knowledge into a contrived image
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites picture-superiority and the multimedia principle, notes the debated mechanism, gives the spatial/sequence/verbal decision rule, and states the coherence caveat against decorative images
revisit_triggers: a controlled card-format A/B (occlusion vs text cloze) result becomes available
a decorative-image coherence problem surfaces in review
a new medium (audio, video) enters the card toolkit

base.update_signal: a card-format A/B result or a coherence problem changes the medium rule

nodes.definition: Set the ordering discipline for composed, multi-step items so a novice can actually learn them. Cognitive load theory: unguided problem-solving overloads working memory; worked examples (Sweller & Cooper 1985, Cognition and Instruction 2(1) 59-89) let novices learn the schema first -- students who studied worked examples solved similar problems in ~half the time with ~1/5 the errors [FACT - snippets]. Caveat -- the expertise-reversal effect: worked examples lose value and can even hurt as expertise grows, so they must be faded out [FACT - snippet]. The prescription: author each multi-step / Apply-Analyze item with its full worked solution FIRST (the schema), then a problem-only variant to fade into as the learner's expertise grows. This is the same chunk mechanism from CHUNKING_LIMITS on the instructional side -- the worked example packages a procedure into a chunk the learner can then deploy. Rule 17 explicitly blesses memorizing the derivation steps themselves.

included: the worked-example benefit (Sweller & Cooper) and the expertise-reversal fade
the worked-solution-first then problem-only authoring order
the tie to the chunk mechanism and Rule-17 derivation-step memorization
excluded: the actual composition of multi-step items from edge chains (RELATIONS_TO_MULTISTEP)

pros.claim: Worked-solution-first authoring lets a novice learn a multi-step schema before being asked to produce it, cutting time and errors

nodes.definition: Stage 1 of the pipeline: parse the TOC and chapter/section boundaries into a sequence of study units, carrying over each section's learning objectives (they arrive Bloom-phrased from TEXTBOOK_ANATOMY) and HOLDING BACK the end-of-chapter questions as a validation set. The chapter order the authors chose already linearizes the prerequisite graph, so 'order' is a cheap first prerequisite approximation the flat representation later reuses. Units are the scheduling/calendar spine regardless of whether a graph is built downstream.

nodes.definition: Stage 2: harvest the terminology layer from each unit -- bold/key terms in the text, the back-of-book glossary definitions, and index hits -- into one record per term: term(id, unit_id, name, definition, image?) [ESTIMATE - design synthesis, HIGH]. This is rung-1 (Remember x Factual) material and the foundation every later stage builds on: claims reference terms, edges connect terms, and an edge card is only well-formed once both endpoint term-cards exist. Heavily-indexed terms are treated as hub nodes (a concept-frequency signal from the index). The glossary supplies ready definitions so the term layer is largely free from the book's own apparatus rather than re-authored.

the term(id,unit_id,name,definition,image?) shape and rung-1 status

nodes.definition: Stage 3: extract atomic factual statements -- one subject, one predicate, one value -- so minimum information is enforced at the DATA level and cards inherit atomicity for free (per MIN_INFO_PRINCIPLE). Stamp each with its source (Rule 18) and a date if the fact is volatile (Rule 19): claim(id, unit_id, text, terms[], source, date?) [ESTIMATE - design synthesis; the Rule 18/19 anchors FACT]. This is rung-2 material. Two honesty disciplines ride here: (a) every claim carries a source id so the coverage-and-honesty gate can trace it, and (b) each claim is tagged FACT / ESTIMATE / UNKNOWN mirroring its grounding, so an UNKNOWN in the source (e.g. an unverified statistic) becomes a claim that names the blocker rather than an invented number. Volatile facts (statistics, prices, guidelines) that are undated silently go stale, so dating them is not optional.

pros.example: storing 'lidocaine blocks Na+ channels [source: ch12, FACT]' as one dated-if-volatile claim the gate can later verify

cons.claim: Atomic extraction is labor-intensive and a mis-split can sever a value from the qualifier that makes it true
cons.example: extracting a dose as a bare number without the patient-weight qualifier, producing a claim that is false out of context

nodes.definition: Stage 4: for every claim that touches >=2 terms, normalize an edge (term_a, relation, term_b, unit_id) -- the concept-map proposition of Novak & Canas 2008 ('two or more concepts connected using linking words to form a meaningful statement'), which is what the owner calls an 'edge' [FACT that propositions are defined that way - snippet; the equation edges~=propositions is ESTIMATE-HIGH, and 'edges' is the owner's own term]. This is rung-3 (Understand x Conceptual) material and simultaneously the (optional) graph's edge set. Examples: (lidocaine, blocks, Na+ channels); (maxillary first molar, has-root-count, 3). The edge table is extracted REGARDLESS of whether a graph is ultimately built, because it is needed for edge cards and it is the reversible pivot between the flat and graph representations. Grounded in Ausubel's meaningful-learning theory: new knowledge attaches to existing cognitive structure, so relations are what bind the terminology into something learnable.

the proposition = owner's 'edge' reading with its honesty tag

excluded: the card family each edge yields (EDGE_CARDS)
the prerequisite/surmise structure over the edges (PREREQ_MAPPING)

pros.example: turning 'the maxillary first molar has 3 roots' into (maxillary first molar, has-root-count, 3) usable as a card and a graph edge

cons.example: labeling a loose association as a causal relation, creating an edge the multi-step stage then over-trusts

failure_modes: inventing a relation the claim does not support
skipping the edge table when the flat representation is chosen and then lacking data for edge cards

nodes.definition: Map the prerequisite structure over the extracted terms and edges, keeping BOTH options live because the owner is unsure about graphs (brief). Option G -- concept graph / knowledge structure: concept maps (Novak & Canas 2008) with labeled linking lines built to answer a focus question [ESTIMATE on the focus-question detail - training knowledge, not snippet-confirmed]; and Knowledge Space Theory (Doignon & Falmagne 1985) where a knowledge STATE is the set of items mastered, a surmise/prerequisite relation (q <= q' iff mastering q' implies q) constrains admissible learning paths, and the FRINGE of a state (items exactly one step ahead) has maximal diagnostic value -- deployed commercially in ALEKS [FACT - snippets]. Option F -- flat units with ordering: chapters/sections are a sequence, prerequisites approximated by 'everything earlier' because the authors already linearized the graph. Graph pros: precise next-item selection (fringe), weakness localization (failed node -> suspect its prerequisites), edge cards fall out directly; cons: expensive to build correctly, brittle if edges are guessed, overkill for linear material [ESTIMATE].

the shared underlying data (terms + edges) that makes the choice reversible
excluded: the final hybrid recommendation and edge-table design (GRAPH_VS_FLAT)

failure_modes: committing to an expensive graph for material the chapter order already linearizes

revisit_triggers: adaptive next-item selection or weakness localization becomes a requirement

base.update_signal: an adaptive-selection requirement or a brittle-edge failure changes the representation options

nodes.definition: Resolve the graph-vs-flat question with the recommended hybrid [ESTIMATE - design recommendation]: flat units as the SPINE (scheduling, progress UI, calendar boxes) PLUS a lightweight edge TABLE (term_a, relation, term_b, unit_id) extracted anyway -- graph-shaped data without graph-dependent machinery. This gives edge cards and cross-chapter relations a home without paying for a full KST engine, and it is upgradeable: adopt full Knowledge Space Theory (fringe-based adaptive selection, weakness localization) ONLY if adaptive selection later demands it. The choice is deliberately reversible because Option G and Option F share the same extracted terms + edges (from CLAIM_TO_RELATIONS), so nothing is thrown away by starting flat. This directly answers the owner's 'graphs, or maybe not the graphs' by not forcing the decision up front: ship the flat spine now, keep the edge table, upgrade on evidence of need.

the reversibility from shared terms+edges data answering the owner's graph uncertainty

nodes.definition: Stage 5: compose 2-3-edge chains and objective-aligned scenarios into Apply/Analyze questions -- the top of the owner's ladder (rung 4/5) [ESTIMATE - design synthesis; anchors FACT]. Chains longer than 2-3 steps are SPLIT into intermediate cards -- Rule 17 explicitly blesses memorizing derivation steps, and the ~4-chunk budget caps how many un-chunked steps one question can demand. These are the exam-style case/vignette items the deck must reach: INBDE-style case items live mostly at Apply/Analyze, so a deck that stops at Remember never reaches them. The composed items align to the section's learning objectives, which is also what the coverage gate checks against the book's own end-of-chapter (often case-based) questions.

nodes.definition: Realize atomic facts and enumerations as cloze cards -- Wozniak Rule 5, the fastest path from source text to items [FACT - snippet]. Anki syntax: wrap hidden text {{c1::hidden}}; {{c2::...}}, {{c3::...}} on the same note generate SEPARATE cards; holding Alt/Option reuses a number so several blanks hide together on one card; nested clozes are supported from Anki 2.1.56 (depth-limited, 3 levels in 24.11) [FACT - snippets citing docs.ankiweb.net and forums]. Quality guardrails [ESTIMATE - direct application of Rules 4/11/12, HIGH]: the deleted span must be SHORT (minimum information); the remaining sentence must UNIQUELY determine the answer (no guessing among similar facts -- interference); keep the surrounding context meaningful, not a bare list skeleton. Cloze is also the documented fix for enumerations (one blank per element, overlapping clozes so each item is cued by its neighbors). The cloze form of an edge ('A <relation> {{c1::B}}.') is one member of the edge-card family.

the short-span / unique-remainder / meaningful-context guardrails

acceptance_tests: the lint enumerates the overloaded/set/enumeration/interference/ambiguous/orphan/undated patterns with the documented fix and Rule anchor each, tags practice-based fixes ESTIMATE, and runs the set-conversion and interference checks deck-wide
revisit_triggers: a new recurring bad-card pattern is observed
a fix's Rule anchor is corrected against the source
a whole-deck check needs re-running after growth

base.update_signal: a new bad-card pattern or a corrected fix anchor updates the lint

nodes.definition: Stage 7, the go/no-go the whole pipeline builds toward [ESTIMATE - design synthesis; anchors FACT]. TWO conditions must both hold. Coverage: the deck must be able to answer the book's OWN end-of-chapter questions (the validation set held back at BOOK_TO_UNITS) -- if it cannot, the decomposition missed content, and the failure LOOPS BACK to the claim/relation extraction stage (TERM_TO_CLAIMS / CLAIM_TO_RELATIONS), not to a cosmetic card edit. Honesty: every card must trace to a claim or edge carrying a source (Rule 18), with volatile facts date-stamped (Rule 19) and each fact tagged FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, so nothing in the deck is an ungrounded assertion. The verdict also confirms the deck climbed to Apply/Analyze (not stalled at Remember) and that the chosen representation (flat spine + edge table, GRAPH_VS_FLAT) is intact. A deck that is coverage-complete but has an untraceable card is a NO-GO until the trace is restored, and vice versa.

included: the coverage condition against the book's EOC questions and the loop-back-to-extraction rule
the honesty condition (source trace, dating, FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tags)
the climb-to-Apply/Analyze and representation-intact confirmations
excluded: the extraction stages the failure loops back to (TERM_TO_CLAIMS/CLAIM_TO_RELATIONS)
the scheduling of the passed deck (scheduler specialist)

pros.claim: A two-part gate makes coverage against the book's own questions and per-card source traceability the joint done-condition, catching both content gaps and ungrounded cards
pros.example: blocking release because the deck cannot answer two chapter questions and one card lacks a source id, and routing the first back to extraction

cons.claim: The book's end-of-chapter questions are an imperfect oracle -- passing them does not prove the deck covers material the book itself omits
cons.example: a deck that answers every chapter question yet misses an exam-relevant concept the textbook never tested

failure_modes: patching a card cosmetically instead of looping a coverage miss back to extraction
passing a deck with an untraceable or untagged card
acceptance_tests: the gate requires the deck to answer the book's EOC questions (looping failures back to extraction) and every card to trace to a sourced, dated-if-volatile, FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN-tagged claim/edge, and confirms the climb to Apply/Analyze and the intact representation
revisit_triggers: a coverage miss loops back and re-opens the extraction stages
an untraceable card is found post-release
the exam/objective set changes what coverage means

base.update_signal: a coverage miss, an untraceable card, or an objective-set change re-opens the gate

edges.why_related: the exploitable chapter skeleton and TOC are what stage 1 parses into units
the chunk budget sets the one-sitting unit size stage 1 targets
the ~4-chunk focus limit is why one card must carry one atomic trace
minimum information is Wozniak Rule 4, drawn from the ruleset
interference control is Rules 11 and 16 of the ruleset
atomic items are still intractable if similar, so interference control extends minimum information
use-imagery (Rule 6) and graphic-deletion (Rule 8) frame the image-vs-text decision
cognitive load from the chunk limit is why novices need worked examples
worked examples sit at the Apply rung the ladder defines
terms are harvested from within the units stage 1 produced
atomic claims are extracted about the harvested terms
claims are atomized at the data level so cards inherit minimum information
claims touching two terms are normalized into edges
the extracted edges are the data the prerequisite structure is mapped over
the hybrid recommendation resolves the graph-vs-flat options laid out in the mapping
multi-step questions are composed from chains of the extracted edges
multi-step items target the Apply/Analyze rungs of the ladder
each multi-step item is authored worked-solution-first per the ordering discipline
the note-type choices and the auto-reverse caution follow from the ruleset (Rule 11)
a well-formed cloze hides a short span so it stays minimum-information
cloze is one of the note types the template mapping assigns
occlusion is chosen only when the medium decision routes knowledge to an image
image occlusion is a special case of cloze deletion on images
each extracted edge is compiled into its relation-card family
the reverse member of an edge card is gated on the interference check
multi-step case items are one of the layers the compile step emits
edge-card families are compiled into the deck
the lint runs over the compiled whole deck
the gate verifies coverage and traceability of the compiled deck
a deck must pass the bad-card lint before the go/no-go verdict
the verdict confirms the chosen flat-spine + edge-table representation is intact
atomic minimum-information pulls to split everything while multi-step synthesis needs items that compose several facts
edges.resolution_rule: keep the atomic claims as the stored data and COMPOSE multi-step items from 2-3 of them, splitting any chain longer than 2-3 steps back into intermediate cards so both atomicity and synthesis hold

edges.why_related: picture-superiority pulls toward more images while the coherence principle warns decorative images add load
edges.resolution_rule: use an image only when it CARRIES the spatial/structural knowledge (occlude load-bearing regions); route verbal-symbolic knowledge to text/cloze and drop merely-decorative images

edges.why_related: auto-reversed cards are convenient to generate but manufacture interference when the back is a shared generic definition
edges.resolution_rule: auto-reverse only when the back UNIQUELY identifies the front; otherwise suppress the reverse or add a discriminating context cue before generating it

edges.why_related: a coverage failure at the gate loops back to re-open claim (and relation) extraction rather than editing the card
the ~4-chunk budget caps a multi-step question at 2-3 un-chunked steps before it must be split
showing the worked solution first causally lowers the load that would otherwise make a novice fail the composed item
the cloze member of the edge-card family is itself a cloze deletion over the relation triple

conflict_axes.name: atomic_min_info_vs_multi_step_synthesis
conflict_axes.description: Minimum information pulls to split every fact into an atomic item, while the top of the ladder needs items that compose several facts into a multi-step inference.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: store atomic claims as the data and compose 2-3-edge multi-step items from them, splitting any chain longer than 2-3 steps back into intermediate cards

conflict_axes.name: graph_richness_vs_flat_simplicity
conflict_axes.description: An explicit concept graph / KST gives precise next-item selection and weakness localization but is expensive and brittle, while flat ordered units are cheap and robust but coarse.
poles: build the full concept graph / KST
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: ship the flat spine plus a lightweight edge table now and upgrade to full KST only if adaptive selection later demands it, since both share the same terms+edges data

conflict_axes.name: image_richness_vs_coherence_load
conflict_axes.description: Picture-superiority evidence pulls toward more images while Mayer's coherence principle warns that decorative images add extraneous load, not memory.
poles: add images for the superiority effect
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use an image only when it carries the spatial/structural knowledge and route verbal-symbolic knowledge to text/cloze, dropping merely-decorative images

conflict_axes.name: auto_reverse_convenience_vs_interference
conflict_axes.description: Auto-generating reversed and edge cards doubles coverage cheaply but manufactures interference when the back does not uniquely identify the front.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: auto-reverse only when the back uniquely identifies the front, otherwise suppress the reverse or add a context cue, and run the interference check across the whole deck

conflict_axes.name: coverage_completeness_vs_deck_size
conflict_axes.description: Covering every claim and objective pulls the deck bigger, while the chunk budget and review-load reality pull toward a lean deck of only load-bearing cards.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cover exactly what the book's end-of-chapter questions and objectives require (Rule 20 prioritize), letting the coverage oracle -- not exhaustiveness -- define done

conflict_axes.name: objective_fidelity_vs_extraction_cost
conflict_axes.description: Faithfully carrying every learning objective and glossary term is thorough but labor-intensive, while a fast pass risks missing content the objectives promised.
poles: extract every objective and term exhaustively
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: lift objectives, bold terms and glossary from the book's own apparatus (cheap fidelity) and prioritize deeper claim extraction where the objectives and index hub-signal point

conflict_axes.name: worked_scaffold_vs_expertise_reversal
conflict_axes.description: Worked-solution-first authoring helps novices but the expertise-reversal effect says the same scaffolds slow or hurt experts.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: author worked-solution-first then a problem-only variant and fade the scaffold as the learner's expertise grows

conflict_axes.name: climb_to_apply_analyze_vs_stall_at_remember
conflict_axes.description: Terminology and single facts are easy to mass-produce (Remember), but exams live at Apply/Analyze, so a deck can feel complete while never climbing.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require the deck to reach multi-step Apply/Analyze items aligned to objectives, treating a Remember-only deck as incomplete at the gate

conflict_axes.name: snippet_confirmed_fact_vs_unverified_verbatim
conflict_axes.description: The Twenty-Rules wording and the current Anki note-type list were confirmed only via search snippets (direct fetch 403-blocked), tempting presentation of reconstructed text as verbatim fact.
poles: quote the reconstructed wording as fact
carry it as snippet-confirmed with the UNKNOWN blocker
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: assert only what a snippet confirmed, flag verbatim wording and the note-type list UNKNOWN with the canonical URL, and defer exact quotation to a fetch-enabled run

edge_cases.description: An overloaded card packs many sub-answers so one grade covers many memory traces and it chronically lapses
edge_cases.trigger: a paragraph or compound fact is compiled as a single card
edge_cases.mitigation: split into atomic items (Rule 4) and keep the same fact from several angles as separate items per Rule 17

edge_cases.description: A 'name the members of X' set is asked as an unordered whole and is virtually un-memorizable
edge_cases.trigger: an unordered collection is turned into one card
edge_cases.mitigation: convert the set into an enumeration (impose an order/grouping) then into overlapping clozes, one element per card

edge_cases.description: An ordered enumeration is asked whole, forcing long serial recall with uneven mastery
edge_cases.trigger: an ordered list is compiled as a single card
edge_cases.mitigation: cloze each element separately with overlapping clozes so each item is cued by its neighbors, and add a mnemonic (Rule 7) for stubborn orders

edge_cases.description: Two similar items keep swapping answers because a per-card review never saw them together
edge_cases.trigger: a confusable pair is compiled without a whole-deck interference check
edge_cases.mitigation: reword for contrast, add a context cue (Rule 16), add an A-vs-B comparison card, and sometimes delete one item

edge_cases.description: An orphan card asks a fact with no understood context so it is rote junk
edge_cases.trigger: a claim is carded before the chapter is understood (violates Rules 1-3)
edge_cases.mitigation: learn the unit first, link the card to prior items (Rule 13), and add a personal example (Rule 14)

edge_cases.description: A volatile statistic or guideline is carded undated and silently goes stale
edge_cases.trigger: a volatile fact is extracted without a date or source stamp
edge_cases.mitigation: date-stamp the fact (Rule 19), source-stamp it (Rule 18), and carry the KB source id on the card

edge_cases.description: An edge card is generated before both endpoint term-cards exist, so it references an unlearned node
edge_cases.trigger: the edge-card stage runs ahead of the term stage for one endpoint
edge_cases.mitigation: gate edge-card generation on both endpoint term-cards existing, per the ladder's prerequisite logic

edge_cases.description: A reversed card's 'question' is a generic definition shared by several terms, manufacturing interference
edge_cases.trigger: auto-reverse is applied where the back does not uniquely identify the front
edge_cases.mitigation: auto-reverse only when the back uniquely identifies the front; otherwise suppress the reverse or add a context cue

edge_cases.description: A multi-step chain longer than 2-3 steps is asked whole and fails on working-memory load, not on logic
edge_cases.trigger: a long derivation is composed into one question
edge_cases.mitigation: split chains longer than 2-3 steps into intermediate cards (Rule 17 blesses memorizing derivation steps) so each item stays within the chunk budget

edge_cases.description: The finished deck cannot answer some of the book's own end-of-chapter questions, revealing missed content
edge_cases.trigger: the coverage oracle is run and an objective's question is unanswerable from the deck
edge_cases.mitigation: loop the failure back to the claim/relation extraction stage and add the missing claims/edges, not a cosmetic card edit

edge_cases.description: A Twenty-Rules heading is quoted as verbatim confirmed text when only its title was snippet-confirmed
edge_cases.trigger: reconstructed wording is presented as the article's exact words
edge_cases.mitigation: assert only snippet-confirmed content, flag verbatim wording and the note-type list UNKNOWN with the canonical URL, and defer exact quotation to a fetch-enabled run

workflow.action: Read the textbook anatomy and identify the exploitable features
workflow.description: Locate the TOC, per-section learning objectives, bold terms, glossary, index and end-of-chapter questions and map each to its downstream artifact
workflow.gate: the front/body/back features are mapped to units/goals/terms/validation-set/hub-signal with the OpenStax FACT and style-manual ESTIMATE tags

workflow.action: Fix the chunk budget for units and card questions
workflow.description: Set the one-sitting unit and ~4-element card-question size limits from Miller and Cowan
workflow.gate: the ~7+/-2 and ~4 limits and the chunk definition are stated and turned into unit and card size rules

workflow.action: Parse the book into sized, ordered units
workflow.description: Cut units at chapter/section boundaries, carry objectives, and reserve the end-of-chapter questions as the validation set
workflow.gate: units are one-sitting sized, carry objectives, and the EOC questions are held back as the coverage oracle

workflow.description: Collect bold terms, glossary definitions and index hits into one record per term
workflow.gate: each term has an id/unit/name/definition record and heavily-indexed terms are marked hub nodes

workflow.description: Break the text into one-subject/one-predicate/one-value claims, stamp source, date volatile facts, and tag FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: claims are atomic, sourced, dated-if-volatile and honesty-tagged

workflow.description: Turn every claim touching two or more terms into a (term_a, relation, term_b, unit_id) edge -- the owner's 'edges'
workflow.gate: every multi-term claim yields an edge and the edge table is extracted regardless of the representation choice

workflow.action: Map prerequisite structure and choose the representation
workflow.description: Lay out the concept-graph/KST option and the flat-units option, then adopt the flat-spine + edge-table hybrid
workflow.gate: both options are presented with graph pros/cons and the hybrid is adopted with full KST deferred until adaptive selection demands it

workflow.description: Chain 2-3 edges into worked-solution-first then problem-only case items aligned to objectives
workflow.gate: items are 2-3 steps, worked-first, and objective-aligned, with longer chains split into intermediate cards

workflow.description: Map terms/claims/relations/multi-step to their note types (basic/reversed/type-in, cloze, occlusion, edge family, case) with a source id on each card
workflow.gate: every layer is compiled to the right note type and each card carries its source claim/edge id

workflow.action: Lint the deck against the bad-card patterns
workflow.gate: each bad-card pattern is detected with its documented fix applied and the interference/set-conversion checks run deck-wide

workflow.description: Verify the deck answers the book's own end-of-chapter questions and every card traces to a sourced claim/edge, looping coverage misses back to extraction
workflow.gate: the deck answers the EOC questions and every card is traceable/dated/honesty-tagged, with coverage failures routed back to claim/relation extraction

dominance_rules.rationale: memorizing un-understood text costs huge time and the knowledge is worthless
dominance_rules.trigger: cards are about to be generated for a unit that has not had a reading/comprehension pass
dominance_rules.action: do the reading pass and link the unit to prior knowledge before carding it

dominance_rules.rationale: the scheduler grades one memory trace, so a card carrying many traces lapses chronically and grades meaninglessly
dominance_rules.trigger: a card would require more than one atomic answer
dominance_rules.action: split it into atomic items and keep redundancy as separate items per Rule 17

dominance_rules.rule: The whole-deck interference check (Rule 11) dominates per-card correctness
dominance_rules.rationale: even simple items are intractable if similar to others, and interference is a relation between items
dominance_rules.trigger: a new or reversed card is added that resembles an existing one
dominance_rules.action: run the deck-wide interference check and reword/context-cue/suppress before shipping

dominance_rules.rule: The book's end-of-chapter questions dominate as the coverage oracle
dominance_rules.rationale: if the deck cannot answer the book's own questions, the decomposition missed content
dominance_rules.trigger: the deck is proposed as complete
dominance_rules.action: test it against the reserved end-of-chapter questions and loop misses back to extraction

dominance_rules.rationale: an unsourced or undated volatile fact silently goes stale and cannot be verified or updated
dominance_rules.trigger: a card lacks a source id, or a volatile fact lacks a date
dominance_rules.action: attach the KB source id and a date stamp, or block the card

dominance_rules.rule: Both endpoint term-cards existing dominates edge-card generation
dominance_rules.rationale: an edge card that references an unlearned node is ill-formed
dominance_rules.trigger: an edge card is about to be generated
dominance_rules.action: confirm both endpoint term-cards exist first, else generate them or defer the edge card

dominance_rules.rule: Snippet-confirmed evidence dominates reconstructed verbatim wording
dominance_rules.rationale: the sources were confirmed via search snippets with direct fetch 403-blocked this session
dominance_rules.trigger: verbatim Twenty-Rules text or the current Anki note-type list is about to be asserted
dominance_rules.action: assert only snippet-confirmed content and flag the verbatim wording UNKNOWN with the canonical URL

dominance_rules.rule: The flat-spine + edge-table hybrid dominates a premature full-graph commitment
dominance_rules.rationale: the owner is unsure about graphs and both options share the same terms+edges data, so starting flat is reversible
dominance_rules.trigger: a full concept graph / KST build is proposed before any adaptive-selection need
dominance_rules.action: ship the flat spine plus the edge table and upgrade to KST only when adaptive selection is actually required

dominance_rules.rule: Climbing to Apply/Analyze dominates stopping at Remember
dominance_rules.rationale: exam-style case items live mostly at Apply/Analyze, so a Remember-only deck is incomplete
dominance_rules.trigger: a deck consists only of terminology and single-fact cards
dominance_rules.action: compose objective-aligned multi-step items before the deck is considered done

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reserve the end-of-chapter questions as the validation set at unit-parsing time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering only at the gate that the coverage oracle was consumed into cards and cannot be used

anti_rework_rules.rule: Atomize and source/date-stamp claims at the data level, not after cards lapse
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-splitting overloaded cards and back-filling sources once chronic lapses appear post-launch

anti_rework_rules.rule: Extract the edge table even when the flat representation is chosen
anti_rework_rules.prevents: having no relation data for edge cards or for a later graph upgrade, forcing a re-extraction

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the interference check across the whole deck at compile time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: confusable pairs shipping and being discovered one-by-one through review failures

anti_rework_rules.rule: Gate edge-card generation on both endpoint term-cards existing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: orphan edge cards that reference unlearned nodes and must be pulled after import

anti_rework_rules.rule: Author each multi-step item worked-solution-first, then a problem-only variant
anti_rework_rules.prevents: novices failing problem-only items and the item being rebuilt with a worked schema later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every claim FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN at extraction time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unverified statistic or reconstructed wording circulating as fact and being retracted from the deck

anti_rework_rules.rule: Cap composed chains at 2-3 steps when authoring, splitting longer ones immediately
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an over-long vignette failing on load and being decomposed into intermediate cards after the fact

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fetch-enabled run verifies the verbatim Twenty-Rules headings/glosses or the current Anki note-type list
iteration_protocol.action: replace the snippet-reconstructed wording with the confirmed text and lift the UNKNOWN blocker

iteration_protocol.trigger: the deck fails to answer one of the book's end-of-chapter questions at the gate
iteration_protocol.action: loop back to claim/relation extraction, add the missing claims/edges, recompile and re-gate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a controlled card-format A/B on image occlusion versus text cloze for anatomy/dental material is published
iteration_protocol.action: update the medium-decision rule and the occlusion-vs-cloze preference from a reasoned default to an evidence-based one

iteration_protocol.trigger: adaptive next-item selection or fine-grained weakness localization becomes a product requirement
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade the flat spine to a full Knowledge Space Theory graph using the retained edge table

iteration_protocol.trigger: a confusable pair keeps swapping answers in review
iteration_protocol.action: reword for contrast, add a context cue or comparison card, and re-run the whole-deck interference check

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new source book with a different or missing pedagogical structure is ingested
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the anatomy feature map and the unit boundaries for that book before extraction

iteration_protocol.trigger: the learner's expertise crosses the point where worked examples begin to slow rather than help
iteration_protocol.action: fade the worked-solution-first items to their problem-only variants

priority_rationale: The textbook anatomy, chunk limit, Bloom ladder and Twenty Rules come first because every extraction and card decision depends on the book's exploitable structure, the working-memory budget, the cognitive-level ladder and the formulation ruleset; the minimum-information, interference, media-choice and worked-example principles next, because they are the discipline the pipeline inherits; the extraction pipeline (book->units->terms->claims->relations) then applies those to the source, with the prerequisite mapping and the flat-vs-graph hybrid resolving the representation the owner was unsure about; the card techniques (templates, cloze, occlusion, edge cards) and the compile step convert the layers into a deck; and the bad-card lint and the coverage-and-honesty gate come last because they operate on the whole compiled deck and compose every upstream output into a defensible go/no-go.
